newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen city to set up large brokerage -- paper.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen city to set up large brokerage -- paper.

text.p: The Shenzhen city government planned to set up the city's largest brokerage to bolster investor confidence in the local securities market, an official press report and local analysts said on Wednesday.
The brokerage, with registered capitalization of up to one billion yuan, would begin operations soon in the southern Chinese city, the official Securities Times reported.

It would be created out of an existing firm, Shenzhen Guotou Securities Co Ltd, a unit of city-owned Shenzhen International Trust and Investment Corp, using funds largely from Shenzhen International and another city-owned firm, Shenzhen Investment Management Co.
As one of the largest in China, the brokerage would help support long-term development of the Shenzhen securities market.
Shenzhen International would be the biggest shareholder in the new brokerage, although its stake was not stated, while Shenzhen Investment would be the second biggest with 30 percent.
The city government has traditionally used Shenzhen International to channel funds into its securities market.
Shenzhen International said earlier this year it would extend up to 500 million yuan in credit to 20 Shenzhen-listed firms which are rated top in terms of 1995 profits and growth.
Analysts said the brokerage would help enliven the market in the run up to neighboring Hong Kong's reversion to Chinese rule.
The government has outlined a blueprint to expand the market and base of local institutional investors over the next nine months, said Zhou Hua, an analyst at China Southern Securities.
